# Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Nigeria, 2024: 1B.6 research note

**Bottom line:** I found **positive anti-proliferation evidence**, but **no public 2024 case** where Tinubu had to stop an ally, proxy, client, or domestic faction from proliferating nuclear capabilities for short-term political gain. The record is mostly **normative and regulatory**: Pelindaba / FMCT support, stronger nuclear safety rules, and tighter nuclear-security coordination.

- [Nigeria Reaffirms Commitment to Treaty of Pelindaba - Badaru](https://defence.gov.ng/2024/09/24/nigeria-reaffirms-commitment-to-treaty-of-pelindaba-badaru/) — Ministry of Defence, Nigeria, September 24, 2024. Claim summary: Nigeria reaffirmed commitment to the Treaty of Pelindaba, called Africa a nuclear-weapon-free zone, and joined a campaign for a fissile-material-cutoff treaty. This is the clearest 2024 evidence for resisting proliferation norms in good faith. Question IDs: `1B.6`, `1B.4`, `1B.1`, `1B.2`

- [President Tinubu Signs Four New Nuclear Safety Regulations](https://www.nnra.gov.ng/nnra/post-president_tinubu_signs_four_new_nuclear_safety_regulations) — Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority, 2024. Claim summary: Tinubu signed four new nuclear safety regulations covering plant design/construction, transport of radioactive material, ionizing radiation, and radioactive waste/spent fuel management. This strengthens domestic controls that reduce the chance of diversion, leakage, or misuse. Question IDs: `1B.6`, `1B.3`, `1B.4`

- [NNRA and IAEA Conducts National Workshop on Transport of Nuclear and Radioactive Materials in Nigeria](https://nnra.gov.ng/nnra/post-nnra_and_iaea_conducts_national_workshop_on_transport_of_nuclear_and_radioactive_materials_in_nigeria) — Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority, May 2024. Claim summary: NNRA and IAEA trained response personnel on transport security for nuclear and radioactive material, explicitly to strengthen security measures during movement and handling. This is indirect but relevant evidence of resisting proliferation pathways and improving custody discipline. Question IDs: `1B.6`, `1B.3`, `1B.4`

- [NNRA and IAEA Kicks Off a Four-Day Review Mission to Evaluate and Strengthen Nigeria’s Nuclear Security Framework](https://nnra.gov.ng/nnra/post-nnra_and_iaea_kicks_off_a_four_day_review_mission_to_evaluate__and_strengthen_nigeria___s_nuclear_security_framework) — Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority, 2024. Claim summary: Nigeria requested an IAEA review mission to strengthen its nuclear security framework and prevent, detect, and respond to nuclear threats. This supports a reading of active resistance to nuclear-risk creation and leakage. Question IDs: `1B.6`, `1B.3`, `1B.4`

## Gap

- I did **not** find a 2024 public example of Tinubu resisting a specific proliferation push by an ally, proxy, client, or domestic faction.
- I also found **no evidence** that such a proliferation attempt was publicly present in Nigeria in 2024.
- So the best-supported conclusion is **general anti-proliferation alignment and tighter controls**, not a documented confrontation with a live proliferation patronage problem.
